turns.text:
As a psychology professor, I'm glad to see you exploring cultural differences! However, it's important to note that my expertise lies more in psychology rather than specific cultural practices or products. That said, I can share that in many Western countries, the most common menstrual products are tampons and sanitary pads. Tampons are inserted into the vagina to absorb menstrual flow, while pads are worn externally in underwear.

In some Asian countries, reusable menstrual cups have gained popularity in recent years. These are silicone or rubber cups that are inserted into the vagina to collect menstrual flow. They are then emptied, cleaned, and reused.

In Africa, traditional methods such as rags, leaves, and banana fibers have been used historically, although more modern products are becoming more available. It's fascinating to see how cultural norms and technological advancements influence the choice of menstrual products! If you're interested, I'd recommend researching how these products impact cultural perceptions of menstruation and women's health.
